Best password managers for emergency access (2026)

By the Afterkeep research team · Reviewed on 15 Oct 2026

Bitwarden is the best password manager for emergency access: affordable, open source and with View or Takeover access. Keeper is a strong alternative. 1Password relies on its Emergency Kit and family recovery. Dashlane no longer has an emergency contact feature.

Key facts

  • #1 Bitwarden: Budget-conscious people who want a proper, tested emergency-access workflow.
  • #2 Keeper: People who want emergency access alongside business-grade security features.
  • #3 Proton Pass (Proton Emergency Access): Proton users who want one emergency process covering Proton Mail, Pass and Drive.
  • #4 LastPass Emergency Access: Existing LastPass users who want to add emergency contacts without switching.
  • #5 1Password: Families who will store the Emergency Kit with their will and use a Families plan, where an organiser can help recover members' accounts.
  • #6 Dashlane: People who use Dashlane for day-to-day passwords and plan legacy access some other way.

Which should you choose?

1. Bitwarden

Best for: Budget-conscious people who want a proper, tested emergency-access workflow.

The best-value password manager with real emergency access: trusted contacts can request View or Takeover access after a wait time you set.

Pricing: Free plan available; Emergency Access requires Premium or a paid Families/Teams/Enterprise plan. Check current pricing.

2. Keeper

Best for: People who want emergency access alongside business-grade security features.

A solid choice with built-in Emergency Access: name trusted contacts who can request your vault after a wait period.

Pricing: Paid plans with a free trial. Check current pricing.

3. Proton Pass (Proton Emergency Access)

Best for: Proton users who want one emergency process covering Proton Mail, Pass and Drive.

A solid privacy-first option: on any paid Proton plan you can name up to five emergency contacts who get access automatically after a wait time you choose, unless you deny the request.

Pricing: Emergency Access is included on all paid Proton plans, including Proton Pass Plus. Check current pricing.

4. LastPass Emergency Access

Best for: Existing LastPass users who want to add emergency contacts without switching.

It works: contacts can request vault access after a wait period. LastPass's 2022 security breaches are a good reason to look at alternatives first, though.

Pricing: Emergency Access is a paid-plan feature. Check current pricing.

5. 1Password

Best for: Families who will store the Emergency Kit with their will and use a Families plan, where an organiser can help recover members' accounts.

Excellent password manager, but it has no automatic emergency-access feature. Legacy planning relies on the Emergency Kit and family account recovery.

Pricing: Paid plans only (free trial). Check current pricing.

6. Dashlane

Best for: People who use Dashlane for day-to-day passwords and plan legacy access some other way.

Not recommended for legacy access. Dashlane removed its Emergency Contact feature and now suggests sharing an exported vault file with a trusted person.

Pricing: Check current pricing.
